description: Hosting layer plus evidence. Snapshot the live Amplify customRules, change scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py so the 15 legacy top-level workspace prefixes answer 302 -> / instead of 301 into the staff Authenticator shell, move the four passthrough rewrites (/api, /get, /r, /mcp) ahead of every redirect so a payment webhook can never be shadowed, add a pytest guard on the rule array and a live probe harness, apply to production with rollback, and write the dated URL/host matrix document. Depends on FEAT-001 only for ordering (the tree must be green before a production write); the code paths do not overlap.
steps: READ FIRST: .agents/tasks/url-host-cleanup/context.json and .agents/tasks/url-host-cleanup/plan.md sections 0.1-0.7, 1 (D1-D5), 2 steps 7-14, 3 (the matrix) and 5 (needs-verification). Also read FEAT-001.json `findings` for the sign-in wiring handoff. Do not re-derive what context.json already states.

Snapshot the live rules to docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-before-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json using `aws amplify get-app --app-id d22dm4b0jn71jw --region us-east-1 --query 'app.customRules' --output json`. Confirm it parses and has 146 entries (re-measure; the count may have drifted, and if it has, record the new number rather than asserting 146). Amplify get-app/update-app expose NO ETag - record that fact in the matrix document instead of inventing one.

CONSUMER INVENTORY BEFORE ANY RULE CHANGE (plan.md step 8a, owner refinement 0.10 item 1 - a blanket purge of the legacy redirect map is FORBIDDEN). For each of the 15 prefixes /dm /engage /dashboard /contacts /commerce /pay /forms /service /docs /seo /admin /access /link /task /settings, record: (i) presence in out/sitemap.xml, public/robots.txt, out/llms.txt or the MCP catalogue; (ii) whether any approved provider artefact names it - cross-check FROZEN_EXTERNAL and the DLT template registry, because an approved DLT or RCS body cannot be edited and a redirect is the only repair there; (iii) search impressions from `.venv/bin/python scripts/retired_url_equity.py --json` over the MAXIMUM window across BOTH Search Console properties (the apex property has no backfill; the 480-day www history holds the equity, and that script's docstring records a 40x under-report from a 90-day window); (iv) in-repo references outside src/pages/workspace/**. Classify each CONVERT / KEEP / NEEDS-OWNER. /access and /admin are CONVERT by explicit owner instruction. If retired_url_equity.py cannot authenticate, say so and classify from (i),(ii),(iv) - do NOT treat an unrunnable measurement as a zero. Put the table in docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md.

DO NOT TOUCH RETIRED, RETIRED_TREES or FROZEN_EXTERNAL in scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py. The legacy content/SEO redirects - /swdhya, /no-fault, /legal-stuff, /legal-stuffs, /faq, /my-order, /expoweek, /ritual-store, /swdhya-store, /request-tracking, /rx-slot, /bring-friends, /home, /open-possibility, /product-page/<*>, /selfservice, /track - are explicitly NOT cleanup targets and must keep redirecting to their existing live targets. Probe every one before and after.

Correct the stale catch-all commentary in src/pages/404.tsx (line ~14 claims the last Amplify rule is /<*> -> /index.html; it is /404.html, which is exactly why this page's noindex and canonical now reach a mistyped URL). Rewrite that paragraph with the measured 2026-10-01 state, keeping the old reading as corrected-in-place history rather than deleting it. Record the four UNOWNED stale sites - src/pages/_app.tsx lines 938, 999, 1098 and src/pages/workspace/commerce/catalog.tsx line 28 - in the matrix document as follow-ups for their owners, and do NOT edit them.

In scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py, add OBSOLETE_PUBLIC_WORKSPACE_PREFIXES holding only the CONVERT keys from the inventory step, and remove those from RENAMED_PREFIXES. Any prefix classified KEEP or NEEDS-OWNER stays in RENAMED_PREFIXES untouched, with a dated comment naming the evidence that kept it there. In desired_redirects(), emit for each CONVERT prefix p three rules at status '302' targeting the literal '/': p, p + '/', and f'{p}/<*>'. STOP emitting the one-hop /dm/calls-style rules for CONVERT prefixes only. Add '/' to LIVE_TARGET_PREFIXES or _targets_dead_prefix() will judge the new rules dead on sight.

Extend is_ours() so EVERY source shape the CONVERT prefixes used to own is still claimed: p, p + '/', f'{p}/<*>', and the one-hop forms (a source starting p + '/' whose /workspace-equivalent is a RETIRED key). This is the step that makes the change stick - apply() preserves anything is_ours() does not claim in `middle`, and provision_legacy_redirects.py documents this exact bug having silently resurrected stale rules twice before. Verify by running the read-only report and confirming no old 301 to /workspace/<prefix> survives in the rebuilt array.

Replace the RENAMED_PREFIXES docstring block with a dated 2026-10-01 note that keeps the old rationale rather than deleting it, and records: the measured defect (14 of the 15 prefixes ended on the staff Authenticator shell at HTTP 200, /settings 301d to a /workspace/settings/ page that 404s); the CONVERT / KEEP / NEEDS-OWNER classification and the evidence behind each, so the next reader does not have to re-measure; that 302 was chosen over deletion because it lands the customer on home with no JavaScript and is reversible per the rollout rule, where falling through to the 404-200 catch-all only reaches home via client-side JS; that the legacy content/SEO map was deliberately left alone on owner instruction; and that staff access is unaffected because /workspace/** is untouched and remains the real entry.

In apply(), partition `keep` into `passthrough` (source starts with '/api', '/get', '/r/' or '/mcp') and the remaining `middle`, and build new_rules = domain + passthrough + desired_redirects() + middle + catch_all. Add a guard that raises BEFORE update_app if any source in desired_redirects() could match /api/, /get/, /r/ or /mcp - provider webhooks are delivered to https://wecare.digital/api/... (razorpay-webhook, webhook/sinch-rcs, webhook/sinch-dlr, wa-business/webhooks, voice-cdr-webhook), so shadowing that rewrite is a payment outage. Do NOT touch the /<*> -> /404.html 404-200 catch-all in any way.

Create tests/test_url_host_routing_rules.py. Load scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py with importlib (the pattern tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py already uses), feed apply() the committed snapshot from step 2 as the live array plus a stub client that captures customRules, and assert on what would be written: (a) no rule targets a path starting '/workspace'; (b) for each of the 15 prefixes, p, p + '/' and p + '/<*>' each target '/' at status '302'; (c) the indices of /api/<*>, /get/<*>, /r/<*> and /mcp are all lower than the index of every 301/302 redirect; (d) the LAST rule is /<*> -> /404.html at 404-200; (e) the FIRST rule is https://www.wecare.digital -> https://wecare.digital at 301. Make no AWS call.

Create scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py. Model the no-redirect opener, thread pool and verdict-per-row shape on scripts/retired_url_probe.py, and reuse the chain-following design of scripts/retired_url_equity.py - trailingSlash:true means an extensionless path always 301s first, so ONLY the terminal status in a chain is meaningful. Encode every row of plan.md section 3 with its expected outcome, support --json and a human table, assert that no row loops (a 302 whose target is '/' must terminate at 200 in one hop), probe POST as well as GET for the /api and /mcp rows, and exit non-zero on any mismatch. Read-only: HTTP GET/POST against the public site only, no AWS write, no secret read. Leave scripts/retired_url_equity.py otherwise UNCHANGED - it is an untracked draft from a closed session and is not this task's to rewrite.

Run the probe BEFORE applying: .venv/bin/python scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py must FAIL on the CONVERT prefix rows and PASS on every RETIRED/FROZEN_EXTERNAL legacy-content row. That failure is the reproduction of the defect and must be captured verbatim into the matrix document as the measured 'before'.

Run the full gate set, then apply: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py tests/test_url_host_routing_rules.py -q. Confirm out/404/index.html still exists and out/sitemap.xml still holds 1,407 <loc> entries (or explain any change). Then .venv/bin/python scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py --apply, followed by --verify and .venv/bin/python scripts/retired_url_probe.py.

Re-probe after applying: .venv/bin/python scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py must exit 0. Independently re-confirm the must-not-break set with curl and record the measured codes: POST /api/razorpay-webhook = 401, POST /api/auth/validate = 401, POST /api/payments/webhook = 404, GET /api/webhook/sinch-rcs = 200, GET /mcp = 405, POST /mcp = 400, GET /get/o/stream/media/m/wecare-digital.png = 200, GET /definitely-not-a-page/ = 404 with "page":"/404" and noindex, https://www.wecare.digital/shop/ = 301 to https://wecare.digital/shop/, /workspace/ = 200 Authenticator shell, /account/sign-in/ = 200, /shop/ /cart/ /orders/ /blog/ = 200. Amplify rule changes are not instant at the CDN - if a row disagrees, wait and re-probe rather than concluding.

Write docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md containing: the section 3 matrix with MEASURED before and after values (never an invented before); the obsolete-public-link inventory from plan.md 0.8 including what was deliberately left alone and why; the domain-coverage inventory from 0.7 with the TLS alert 40 evidence, the one-label-only certificate limit, and the two second-label Wix hosts (xout, www.xout) as out of scope; the exact subdomain work NOT done, framed as an owner-decision item needing BOTH an Amplify update-domain-association with prefix '*' AND a Route 53 *.wecare.digital alias, with the blast radius stated (the association mutation targets the domain serving the canonical home, and DNS without the association resolves typos to a host CloudFront refuses at TLS); the _routes.json no-consumer finding from 0.1 and that the file was deliberately left byte-identical; the unknown-API-route 302 -> /contact/ finding from 0.6 marked as owned by the amplify/functions workstream; the public/sw.js item marked needs-verification-during-implementation; the ready-to-apply one-line wiring for src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx from FEAT-001 findings, naming src/pages/account/** as the owning workstream; and the rollback procedure `aws amplify update-app --app-id d22dm4b0jn71jw --region us-east-1 --custom-rules file://docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-before-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json` with the no-ETag note.

Commit by explicit path on branch stack. The index may already hold another session's staged work, so use: git add <new files> && git commit --only <every owned path touched by FEAT-001 and FEAT-002> -F <message file in .scratch/>. Never git add . / -A / -u, never bare git stash, never --amend, no force push. Then git push origin stack.

Set this feature's status to 'completed' in this file and record in `findings`: the live rule count before and after, the applied-at timestamp, every probe row whose measured value differed from the expectation, and anything left open for the owner.
acceptance_criteria: docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-before-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json exists, parses, and holds the pre-change rule array with its count recorded.
Every one of the 15 legacy prefixes carries a CONVERT / KEEP / NEEDS-OWNER classification with its evidence in docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md, and /access plus /admin are CONVERT.
Each CONVERT prefix plus its '/' and '/<*>' forms targets '/' at status 302; no CONVERT rule targets a path starting /workspace.

Every RETIRED / RETIRED_TREES / FROZEN_EXTERNAL source still redirects to its existing live target, probed before and after - including /swdhya, /no-fault, /legal-stuff, /faq, /my-order, /product-page/partner, /selfservice and /track. The legacy content/SEO map is byte-identical in scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py.
src/pages/404.tsx's stale '/index.html' catch-all paragraph is corrected to the measured /404.html state, and the four unowned stale sites are recorded as follow-ups rather than edited.
/api/<*>, /get/<*>, /r/<*> and /mcp all appear before every redirect rule, and the final rule is still /<*> -> /404.html at 404-200.
.venv/bin/python scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py exits 0 after the apply, with every plan.md section 3 after-row matching.

Measured and unchanged after the apply: POST /api/razorpay-webhook = 401, POST /api/auth/validate = 401, GET /mcp = 405, POST /mcp = 400, GET /get/o/stream/media/m/wecare-digital.png = 200, GET /definitely-not-a-page/ = 404 with "page":"/404", https://www.wecare.digital/shop/ = 301 to the apex /shop/, /workspace/ = 200 Authenticator shell, /account/sign-in/ = 200.
.venv/bin/python scripts/retired_url_probe.py stays green - no retired public URL answers 200.
npm run build succeeds and out/404/index.html still exists.
_routes.json is byte-identical to its pre-task state (git diff reports no change).
No DNS record, ACM certificate, CloudFront distribution, domain association, WAF or Security Hub setting was created, modified or deleted.
docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md contains the full matrix with measured before AND after values, the exact subdomain coverage gap, and the rollback command.
The commit lists only owned paths (git show --stat HEAD), and the other session's modified files are not in it.
verification: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build
git show --stat HEAD  (must list only owned paths)
findings:
COMPLETE 2026-10-01, under OPTION B as decided by the parent session after this feature was paused for a product decision. Commits d7dc0103 (6 owned paths) and 2ec84830 (1 path) on branch stack. NOT PUSHED - the parent pushes.

=== WHY THIS FEATURE DID NOT DO WHAT IT SAYS ===
FEAT-002 as written was SUPERSEDED before implementation. Another session had already executed an explicit owner instruction, 'delete all url redirects now' (docs/execution/url-redirect-removal-20261001.md), removing 138 of 146 custom rules from production and rewriting scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py so desired_redirects() returns []. That made four of this feature's acceptance criteria unsatisfiable and one of its core steps a direct reversal of a newer owner decision:
  - step 6 (emit 45 rules at 302 -> /) would recreate redirects the owner retired;
  - the criterion that all 17 RETIRED/RETIRED_TREES/FROZEN_EXTERNAL sources still redirect is false - all 17 are 404 now, by owner instruction;
  - the criterion that the first rule is the www -> apex 301 was false - it had been deleted;
  - the criterion that the legacy map is byte-identical in the provisioner was false - that file had been gutted.
The defect FEAT-002 existed to fix was ALREADY CLOSED, by deletion rather than by conversion: all 15 legacy prefixes now terminate at 404 instead of on the staff Authenticator shell at 200. Paused with severity warning; parent chose OPTION B.

=== LIVE RULE COUNT: BEFORE AND AFTER ===
  146  before the owner's removal (another session; snapshot amplify-custom-rules-before-owner-removal-20261001.json, not mine, left uncommitted as theirs)
    8  after their removal = the BEFORE for this feature. Snapshotted to docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-before-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json, parses, 8 entries, statuses {200, 404-200}.
    9  after this feature. Snapshotted to docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-after-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json.
Diffed, not assumed: +1 added, -0 removed, 0 reordered; after[1:] == before exactly.
Amplify get-app/update-app expose NO ETag - recorded in the matrix doc rather than inventing one.

=== APPLIED-AT ===
2026-10-01T08:59:52Z (2026-10-01T14:29:52+05:30). One rule, restored VERBATIM from the 146-rule snapshot: {source: 'https://www.wecare.digital', target: 'https://wecare.digital', status: '301'}, inserted first. Readback: 9 rules, host rule first, /<*> -> /404.html 404-200 last.
WHY: the removal deleted the www -> apex 301 as collateral, so the entire site was served at 200 under a second hostname. Measured before restoring: www / = 200, www /shop/ = 200. After: 301 -> apex, PATH PRESERVED (www /shop/ -> apex /shop/, not apex home), because source and target are bare origins with no path component.

=== PROBE ROWS THAT DIFFERED FROM THE WRITTEN EXPECTATION (all because of the owner's removal, none a regression) ===
  1. The 15 legacy prefixes x3 shapes: plan expected 302 -> /. MEASURED 404 (bare form 301 to add the slash, then 404). Defect closed, differently.
  2. /dm/calls and /admin/anything/deep: plan expected 302 -> /. MEASURED 301 -> slash -> 404.
  3. All 17 RETIRED/RETIRED_TREES/FROZEN_EXTERNAL sources: plan expected 'unchanged 301 to live targets'. MEASURED 404, every one - including /swdhya/ /no-fault/ /legal-stuff/ /faq/ /my-order/ /product-page/partner/ /selfservice/ /track/.
  4. www rows: plan recorded BEFORE as '301 -> apex'. MEASURED BEFORE as 200 (the regression this feature fixed). AFTER matches the plan.
  5. HEAD www / returned 200 with x-cache Hit, age 1501, ~25 min after the apply, while GET returned 301 Miss. A stale edge object (apex carries s-maxage=31536000 and the cache key ignores the query string, so a cache-bust did not shift it). It EXPIRED ON ITS OWN - HEAD and GET now both 301 on / and /shop/, five consecutive attempts, all cache Miss. No invalidation created.
EVERYTHING ELSE MATCHED: 85 rows probed, 0 failed, exit 0, no loops. POST /api/razorpay-webhook 401, POST /api/auth/validate 401, POST /api/payments/webhook 404, POST /api/wa-business/webhooks 401, GET /api/webhook/sinch-rcs 200, GET /mcp 405, POST /mcp 400, GET /get/o/... 200, /r miss 302 -> /contact/ -> 200, /definitely-not-a-page/ 404 with "page":"/404" + noindex asserted in the body, /404/ 200, /workspace/ 200, /workspace/access/ 200, /account/sign-in/ 200, 12 public pages 200, shop.wecare.digital no TCP connection, xout 404, mta-sts 403. Also measured but not in the plan: GET /api/webhook/sinch-dlr 404, POST /api/voice-cdr-webhook 404 (API-side routing answers through the intact rewrite).

=== FILES ===
CREATED: docs/execution/snapshots/amplify-custom-rules-{before,after}-url-host-cleanup-20261001.json; docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md; scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py (85 rows, terminal-status-only, seen-set loop detection, GET+POST, --json/--only, read-only); tests/test_url_host_routing_rules.py (11 tests).
MODIFIED: src/pages/404.tsx - stale catch-all comment corrected in place with the old reading kept as dated history, plus what the removal changed (that page is now the destination for ~150 retired aliases rather than a long-tail safety net).
NOT TOUCHED, as instructed: scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py and tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py (the other session's, left exactly as they left them); _routes.json (git diff empty); amplify/**, src/pages/account/**, src/lib/customerAuth.ts, src/lib/dialCodes.ts, src/components/HeaderCart.tsx, src/components/PhoneField.tsx, docs/execution/checkout-c1-c7-closure-matrix-20261001.md; src/lib/seo-page-prompt.ts, src/components/seo/InstructionsContent.tsx, src/content/products.ts (another session's).
NOT CREATED: the 45 redirect rules. Deliberate - see above.

=== GATES, exact tree ===
npm run typecheck 0. npm run lint 0 errors / 188 warnings (pre-existing baseline, count unmoved). npx vitest run 47 files / 674 tests passed. npm run build green, out/404/index.html present (36,567 bytes), out/sitemap.xml 1,407 <loc> unchanged. pytest tests/test_url_host_routing_rules.py tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py -q = 14 passed. scripts/probe_url_host_matrix.py exit 0. scripts/retired_url_probe.py exit 0 - and note it holds 'www must 301 to the apex', so between the removal and this change it was FAILING on that row (a 200 classifies STILL-LIVE, exit 1); independent confirmation from a file this feature did not write. git diff --stat _routes.json empty.
TWO NON-ZERO EXITS, BOTH PREDICTED: scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py (no flag) exits 1 reporting '9 rules; 1 redirects to remove', and --verify exits 1 with 'FAIL: custom redirect rules remain'. See hazard 3 below.

=== OPEN FOR THE OWNER (3 items, all recorded in docs/execution/url-host-matrix-20261001.md) ===
1. /selfservice (1,128 impressions, the largest single figure) and /track are printed inside approved provider template bodies that CANNOT be edited - DLT SMS template ivr-default (registration 1007277993798259629) and nine approved Sinch RCS templates including rcsmenu, the only one any code sends; /track is in approved wecare_order_update. A redirect was their ONLY possible repair and they now 404, so a recipient following a link in a message already sent reaches the missing-page document. The owner's removal document acknowledges this, so it is accepted rather than an oversight. Reversing it is two rules and one instruction; both targets (/submit-request/, /orders/) measured 200 today.
2. Wildcard subdomain coverage NOT done. Needs BOTH an Amplify update-domain-association with prefix '*' AND a Route 53 *.wecare.digital A+AAAA alias. Step 1 mutates the live association serving the canonical home and can move the domain out of AVAILABLE; step 2 WITHOUT step 1 is worse than today's clean no-address, because every typo'd subdomain would then resolve to a host CloudFront refuses at TLS (measured: alert 40 handshake_failure for shop.wecare.digital, apex 200 through the same IP). The certificate is NOT the gap - SAN covers wecare.digital and *.wecare.digital to 2027-03-11 - but *.wecare.digital matches ONE label only, so a second-label host needs a new SAN re-associated on both the Amplify app AND CloudFront E1SZBXLQ4XNLJ7, the MTA-STS policy endpoint under mode: enforce. xout.wecare.digital and www.xout.wecare.digital are existing second-label Wix hosts, out of scope.
3. KNOWN HAZARD, pinned by test rather than fixed: the rewritten provisioner's is_ours() claims any status in {301,302,307,308,404}, so the host rule is a 301 and `--apply` WILL DELETE IT, silently restoring the duplicate-host state, while `--verify` exits 1 while it is live. Not fixed because the fix means editing another session's uncommitted file AND its test, which explicitly lists this same rule among those it expects removed. BOUNDED: .github/workflows/public-surface-deploy.yml is workflow_dispatch only, so nothing runs it on push. tests/test_url_host_routing_rules.py::test_the_provisioner_would_strip_the_host_rule_KNOWN_HAZARD asserts the behaviour and says to INVERT it, not delete it, when someone fixes it.
ALSO RECORDED, not acted on: _routes.json has zero code consumers and is left byte-identical; GET /api/definitely-no-route 302 -> /contact/ from the HTTP API's GET /{code} catch-all, owned by the amplify/functions workstream and asserted at its measured value so a change becomes visible; public/sw.js:180 push-click default /workspace/dashboard/ still needs-verification (not reproduced as customer-reachable, changing it could break staff push); four stale catch-all comments at src/pages/_app.tsx:938,999,1098 and src/pages/workspace/commerce/catalog.tsx:28 handed to their owners unedited; and FEAT-001's ready-to-apply one-line sign-in wiring carried verbatim into section 7 of the matrix doc, naming src/pages/account/** as the owning workstream and the two behaviour changes that owner must accept first.

=== PROHIBITIONS HONOURED ===
No DNS change of any kind (no MX, _mta-sts TXT, SPF, DMARC, DKIM, TLS-RPT). No ACM change. No cloudfront update-distribution and no invalidation. No amplify update-domain-association. No WAF. No Security Hub. Nothing deleted - no hosted-zone record, distribution, bucket, Lambda or IAM entity. No secretsmanager get-secret-value or batch-get-secret-value. No credential on any command line or in any log. The /<*> -> /404.html 404-200 catch-all untouched. _routes.json byte-identical. scripts/retired_url_equity.py not rewritten (it DID authenticate and run: 13,756 recoverable impressions, 0 errors, and it is the source of every impression figure in the matrix). Exactly ONE production write: the update-app documented above.
